newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in heavy trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Monday on very high volume as new money moved into the market, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.99 percent, or 2.38 points, to 280.53 on heavy all-share turnover of 220 million shekels against 195 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.71 percent higher at 288.10.

"After four difficult years the market is recovering and it looks like a one-way ticket. This is only the beginning of a positive trend that we expect to continue," said Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
"Right now there is no negative information and things can only improve. The main indicator for the change in the market is the recovery of the primary market," Mizrahi added.
He said most of the money is coming from investors increasing the weighting of shares in their protfolios. "The genral public is still outside," he said.
A trader at the First International Bank of Israel added that the mutual funds had raised considerable money in the last few weeks, which is now entering the market and lifting prices.
"The mood is very positive. We might see a technical correction in the near term, but it is expected to be a very moderate one," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which gained 0.5 percent to 540 agorot on volume of 21.6 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.0 percent to 797 agorot on turnover of 9.4 million shekels; and Discount Investment Corp, which fell 1.75 percent to 29,479 agorot on volume of 9.0 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
